national.pledge: Campaign Back Pocket Boost: raise income-tax thresholds and deliver middle-income tax relief.
national.outcome: Budget 2024 raised personal thresholds from 31 July 2024 and expanded related credits, largely matching the campaign package with coalition funding adjustments.

national.pledge: Repeal Labour Three Waters / Affordable Water reforms.
national.outcome: Water Services Acts Repeal Act 2024 repealed the entity model in February 2024; Local Water Done Well replacement legislation continued to roll out afterward.

national.pledge: Reduce the residential bright-line test from 10 years to 2 years.
national.outcome: Legislation reinstated a 2-year bright-line test applying to disposals with a bright-line end date on or after 1 July 2024.

national.pledge: Fund part of tax relief via a foreign residential buyers tax while keeping the foreign-buyer ban.
national.outcome: National-NZ First coalition agreement stopped the foreign buyers tax; tax relief was funded through other savings and revenue measures instead.

national.pledge: End the Clean Car Discount (feebate) scheme.
national.outcome: Land Transport (Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme Repeal) Amendment Act 2023 repealed the scheme in the government's early agenda.

national.pledge: As opposition, oppose Labour Auckland light rail delivery failures and argue the project should not proceed as promised.
national.outcome: Auckland light rail was not built in the 2020-23 term; the competing-bid process stalled and construction never started before the 2023 election.

national.pledge: Cancel Auckland Light Rail and reprioritise Auckland transport investment.
national.outcome: Cabinet cancelled the Auckland Light Rail project in December 2023; the delivery company was wound up and no track was built under that project.

national.pledge: 2008 campaign: deliver National personal income-tax cuts and related threshold changes early in a National-led government.
national.outcome: Taxation (Urgent Measures and Annual Rates) legislation in December 2008 implemented National's income-tax package.

national.pledge: Budget 2010 tax switch: raise GST to 15% from 1 October 2010 and cut personal income-tax rates, with compensation.
national.outcome: GST rose to 15% and personal tax rates were reduced from 1 October 2010 with compensation adjustments.

national.pledge: Introduce 90-day trial periods for new employees as a pre-election employment-relations commitment.
national.outcome: Employment Relations Amendment Act 2008 created statutory 90-day trial provisions from 1 March 2009 for smaller employers.

national.pledge: 2008 election: invest Crown capital to accelerate ultra-fast broadband fibre rollout for most New Zealanders.
national.outcome: Government finalised the UFB initiative, signed Crown Fibre partner deals, and began physical rollout from 2010.

national.pledge: 2011 election: extend mixed ownership — sell up to 49% of selected energy SOEs while keeping majority Crown control.
national.outcome: MOM legislation passed; IPOs proceeded for Mighty River, Meridian and Genesis; Solid Energy never reached IPO (partial programme).

national.pledge: As opposition, oppose a broad capital gains tax and commit that National would not introduce one.
national.outcome: In April 2019 the Labour-led government abandoned CGT for lack of coalition consensus; no comprehensive CGT was enacted that term.

national.pledge: Pledge to reverse Labour's ban on new offshore oil and gas exploration permits if returned in 2020.
national.outcome: National did not win 2020; Crown Minerals (Petroleum) Amendment Act 2018 kept the offshore ban through this window.

labour.pledge: Introduce a 39% top personal income-tax rate on income over $180,000.
labour.outcome: Taxation (Income Tax Rate and Other Amendments) legislation applied the 39% rate from the 2021-22 income year.

labour.pledge: 2020 campaign ruled out a capital gains tax and a wealth tax for that term.
labour.outcome: No CGT or wealth tax was introduced 2020-23; revenue focus stayed on the 39% rate and other measures.

labour.pledge: Deliver Auckland light rail (flagship transport/housing-linked promise carried from 2017 into later terms).
labour.outcome: No light rail was built; the twin-track process ended without an agreed route or construction start in the term.

labour.pledge: Expand public and transitional housing places via the Public Housing Plan / Kainga Ora build programme.
labour.outcome: Thousands of additional public and transitional places were added, but original KiwiBuild-scale private supply targets from earlier years were not met.

labour.pledge: Pass Three Waters / Affordable Water reform legislation.
labour.outcome: Reform legislation was enacted in the term; it was later repealed by the 2023-26 government.

labour.pledge: Oppose ACT Treaty Principles Bill and call for it to be blocked.
labour.outcome: Labour opposed the bill; Parliament defeated it at second reading in April 2025 (112-11).

labour.pledge: Introduce Fair Pay Agreements for sector-wide bargaining on pay and conditions.
labour.outcome: Fair Pay Agreements Act 2022 received royal assent and the system commenced in December 2022 (later repealed by the 2023-26 government).

labour.pledge: Pass smoked-tobacco endgame law including smokefree generation, retail reduction and denicotinisation.
labour.outcome: Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products (Smoked Tobacco) Amendment Act 2022 passed; the three core measures were later repealed in 2024.

labour.pledge: Budget 2005 / campaign: introduce KiwiSaver workplace retirement savings with government kick-start from 1 July 2007.
labour.outcome: KiwiSaver commenced 1 July 2007 with kick-start and matching support as delivered family-policy package.

labour.pledge: 2005 election pledge: no further interest on student loans for eligible NZ-resident borrowers from 1 April 2006.
labour.outcome: Student Loan Scheme Amendment Act 2005 implemented interest write-offs for eligible resident borrowers from 1 April 2006.

labour.pledge: Fund 20 hours free early childhood education per week for three- and four-year-olds from July 2007.
labour.outcome: 20 Hours Free ECE took effect 1 July 2007 with large service and child uptake at launch.

labour.pledge: Establish a national emissions trading scheme to price greenhouse gas emissions.
labour.outcome: Climate Change Response (Emissions Trading) Amendment Act 2008 received royal assent 25 September 2008.

labour.pledge: As opposition, campaign to stop National's partial privatisation of state-owned energy companies.
labour.outcome: Partial sales of Mighty River, Meridian and Genesis proceeded; a 2013 citizens-initiated referendum opposed sales but did not stop them.

labour.pledge: 2017 campaign: first year of provider-based tertiary study fees-free for eligible new students from 2018.
labour.outcome: Fees Free began 1 January 2018; early Beehive reporting showed tens of thousands of learners on fees-free.

labour.pledge: 2017 Families Package: Best Start, Winter Energy Payment, Working for Families and accommodation changes.
labour.outcome: Families Package legislation passed; Best Start and related measures commenced mid-2018.

labour.pledge: Ban non-resident foreign buyers from purchasing existing NZ homes; strengthen Overseas Investment Act.
labour.outcome: Overseas Investment Amendment Act 2018 restricted overseas purchases of existing residential land from October 2018.

labour.pledge: KiwiBuild: 100,000 affordable homes for first-home buyers within ten years.
labour.outcome: By late 2019 the 100,000 target was reset/abandoned; completed KiwiBuild homes were far below interim targets.

labour.pledge: End new offshore oil and gas exploration permits as part of a low-carbon transition.
labour.outcome: April 2018: no further offshore petroleum exploration permits; Block Offer limited to onshore Taranaki; existing permits honoured.

green.pledge: As confidence-and-supply partner, advance Zero Carbon Act goals including clean vehicle uptake measures.
green.outcome: Clean Car Discount / clean vehicle settings were introduced in 2021-22 under the Labour-Greens support arrangement; later repealed after 2023.

green.pledge: Price agricultural greenhouse gas emissions (farm-level system targeted by mid-2020s via He Waka Eke Noa pathway).
green.outcome: Policy design and Cabinet work progressed, but farm-level pricing was not operating by the 2023 election and was later paused/reversed by the new government.

green.pledge: Campaign for a wealth tax; seek progress while supporting a Labour government.
green.outcome: Labour ruled out a wealth tax for the term; no wealth tax was enacted.

green.pledge: Oppose the Treaty Principles Bill and mobilise against it.
green.outcome: Greens opposed the bill alongside Labour and Te Pati Maori; it was defeated at second reading in April 2025.

green.pledge: Oppose repeal of the 2022 smoked-tobacco endgame measures.
green.outcome: Greens voted against repeal; the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Amendment Act 2024 still removed the generation ban, retail cut and denicotinisation settings.

green.pledge: Confidence-and-supply: introduce a Zero Carbon Act and independent Climate Commission.
green.outcome: Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Act received royal assent in November 2019, establishing the Climate Change Commission.

green.pledge: C&S agreement: overhaul welfare — improve access, review sanctions, and lift incomes.
green.outcome: Welfare Expert Advisory Group reported in 2019; some benefit and sanction changes followed, but a full overhaul was not completed by 2020.

green.pledge: C&S agreement: hold a referendum on legalising personal-use cannabis by the 2020 election.
green.outcome: 2020 referendum held; official result was No — Cannabis Legalisation and Control Bill not enacted.

green.pledge: As opposition, support a citizens-initiated referendum against partial asset sales.
green.outcome: 2013 referendum returned a large No majority, but the National government continued remaining sales.

act.pledge: Introduce a Treaty Principles Bill based on ACT policy (coalition: support to select committee).
act.outcome: Bill was introduced and supported to select committee; National and NZ First opposed at second reading and it was defeated 112-11 in April 2025.

act.pledge: Restore Three Strikes sentencing legislation (National-ACT coalition commitment).
act.outcome: Sentencing (Reinstating Three Strikes) Amendment Act 2024 passed; regime in force from 17 June 2025.

act.pledge: Flatten / simplify the personal income-tax scale.
act.outcome: Finance Minister engaged ACT on flattening for Budget 2024 but did not implement it; National-shaped threshold relief proceeded instead.

act.pledge: Repeal the Clean Car Discount (National-ACT coalition item).
act.outcome: Scheme repealed by Land Transport (Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme Repeal) Amendment Act 2023.

act.pledge: As opposition, oppose Three Waters co-governance and centralisation reforms.
act.outcome: Three Waters / Affordable Water legislation still passed under Labour; ACT's opposition did not stop enactment in that term.

act.pledge: Reintroduce charter schools / kura hourua (National-ACT coalition commitment).
act.outcome: Education and Training Amendment Act 2024 restored a statutory charter-school framework.
Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Amendment Act 2024 removed retail reduction, denicotinisation and generation-ban provisions.

act.pledge: As opposition after the March 2019 Christchurch attacks, ACT argued for a more carefully scoped firearms response and against rushed reform without adequate select-committee process.
act.outcome: Arms (Prohibited Firearms, Magazines, and Parts) Amendment Act 2019 passed under urgency with broad support; ACT's preferred slower pathway was not adopted.

act.pledge: 2008 confidence-and-supply: enact ACT's three-strikes regime for repeat serious offenders.
act.outcome: National and ACT agreed a three-strikes model in the Sentencing and Parole Reform Act 2010.
Education Amendment Act 2013 inserted partnership schools provisions; first schools opened in subsequent years.

act.pledge: 2008 National-ACT agreement: establish taskforces to review base government spending sector by sector.
act.outcome: Government launched fundamental spending reviews on policy advice tied to the National-ACT agreement.

nz-first.pledge: Coalition demand: progress National tax relief without a foreign residential buyers tax / without repealing the foreign-buyer ban for that purpose.
nz-first.outcome: National-NZ First agreement excluded the foreign buyers tax; Budget 2024 funded relief via other measures.

nz-first.pledge: Repeal 2022 smokefree smoked-tobacco amendments (denicotisation, retail cuts, generation ban) before March 2024.
nz-first.outcome: Coalition progressed repeal of the Smokefree Environments smoked-tobacco amendments; associated Cabinet papers document delivery of the agreement.

nz-first.pledge: Stop first-year Fees Free and replace with final-year Fees Free (no change before 2025).
nz-first.outcome: Coalition agreements locked in switching Fees Free to the final year with the delayed start; implementation followed the agreement timetable.

nz-first.pledge: Support ACT Treaty Principles Bill only to select committee, not as enduring NZ First policy.
nz-first.outcome: NZ First supported the bill to select committee then opposed progression; bill failed second reading in April 2025.

nz-first.pledge: Support disestablishing Te Aka Whai Ora (Maori Health Authority) as part of the coalition health reset.
nz-first.outcome: Pae Ora (Disestablishment of Maori Health Authority) Amendment Act 2024 disestablished the authority (effective 30 June 2024).

nz-first.pledge: Coalition agreement: Regional Development / Provincial Growth Fund of about $1 billion a year.
nz-first.outcome: Cabinet established the PGF in late 2017; fund opened for applications in 2018 with multi-year funding committed.

nz-first.pledge: Coalition agreement: stop non-resident foreigners buying existing houses; strengthen Overseas Investment Act.
nz-first.outcome: Overseas Investment Amendment Act 2018 introduced residential land screening from October 2018.

nz-first.pledge: Coalition agreement: progressively raise the adult minimum wage toward $20 per hour.
nz-first.outcome: Adult minimum wage reached $20.00/hour from 1 April 2021 via Minimum Wage Order.

nz-first.pledge: As opposition, commit to buy back shares in privatised SOEs at no more than the original sale price.
nz-first.outcome: Partial SOE sales completed under National; NZ First was not in government and did not buy back sold stakes before 2017.

te-pati-maori.pledge: Champion a Maori Health Authority / stronger Maori health leadership structures.
te-pati-maori.outcome: Te Aka Whai Ora (Maori Health Authority) was established under Pae Ora reforms during the Labour-led term.

te-pati-maori.pledge: Oppose disestablishment of the Maori Health Authority.
te-pati-maori.outcome: Pae Ora (Disestablishment of Maori Health Authority) Amendment Act 2024 disestablished Te Aka Whai Ora despite opposition protests.

te-pati-maori.pledge: Oppose the Treaty Principles Bill and support Hiiikoi mo te Tiriti mobilisation.
te-pati-maori.outcome: Te Pati Maori opposed the bill; Parliament defeated it at second reading in April 2025.

te-pati-maori.pledge: Remove GST from food (members bill / campaign priority).
te-pati-maori.outcome: GST remains on food nationally; Te Pati Maori continued advocacy and members-bill pressure without government enactment.

te-pati-maori.pledge: Pass a members bill letting Maori electors switch freely between Maori and general rolls.
te-pati-maori.outcome: Electoral (Right to Switch Rolls Freely) Amendment Bill was defeated at first reading in November 2022.

te-pati-maori.pledge: As National-led support partner (Maori Party), advance Whanau Ora / whanau-centred services (2008 confidence-and-supply).
te-pati-maori.outcome: Budget 2010 funded Whanau Ora; programme launched with a responsible minister; later commissioning agencies established (continuity caveat: Maori Party lineage to Te Pati Maori).

te-pati-maori.pledge: Review and replace the Foreshore and Seabed Act 2004 while protecting public access (2008 C&S).
te-pati-maori.outcome: Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Act 2011 repealed the 2004 Act and restored a customary marine title pathway.

te-pati-maori.pledge: Continue constitutional review / advisory panel work arising from Maori Party–National relationship accords.
te-pati-maori.outcome: Constitutional Advisory Panel reported in 2013 recommending ongoing conversation; no major entrenchment reforms enacted.
